In [[linear algebra]], the '''Dieudonné determinant''' is a generalization of the [[determinant]] of a [[matrix (mathematics)|matrix]] to matrices over [[division ring]]s and [[local ring]]s. It was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Dieudonné|authorlink=Jean Dieudonné|year=1943}}.

If ''K'' is a division ring, then the Dieudonné determinant is a [[group homomorphism]] from the [[group (mathematics)|group]] GL<sub>''n''</sub>(''K''{{hairsp}}) of [[invertible matrix|invertible]] ''n''-by-''n'' matrices over ''K''  onto the [[abelianization]] ''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>/{{hairsp}}[''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>,&thinsp;''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>] of the multiplicative group ''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup> of ''K''.

For example, the Dieudonné determinant for a 2-by-2 matrix is the residue class, in ''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>/{{hairsp}}[''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>,&thinsp;''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>], of

:<math>\det \left({\begin{array}{*{20}c} a & b \\ c & d \end{array}}\right) = 
\left\lbrace{\begin{array}{*{20}c} -cb & \text{if } a = 0 \\ ad - aca^{-1}b & \text{if } a \ne 0. \end{array}}\right. </math>

==Properties==
Let ''R'' be a local ring.  There is a determinant map from the [[matrix ring]] GL(''R''{{hairsp}}) to the abelianised [[unit group]] ''R''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup><sub>ab</sub> with the following properties:<ref name=Ros64>Rosenberg (1994) p.64</ref>
* The determinant is invariant under [[elementary row operation]]s
* The determinant of the [[identity matrix]] is 1
* If a row is left multiplied by ''a'' in ''R''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup> then the determinant is left multiplied by ''a''
* The determinant is multiplicative: det(''AB'') = det(''A'')det(''B'')
* If two rows are exchanged, the determinant is multiplied by −1
* If ''R'' is [[commutative ring|commutative]], then the determinant is invariant under [[transpose|transposition]]

==Tannaka–Artin problem==
Assume that ''K'' is finite over its [[center (ring theory)|center]] ''F''.  The [[reduced norm]] gives a homomorphism ''N''<sub>''n''</sub> from GL<sub>''n''</sub>(''K''{{hairsp}}) to ''F''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>.  We also have a homomorphism from GL<sub>''n''</sub>(''K''{{hairsp}}) to ''F''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup> obtained by composing the Dieudonné determinant from GL<sub>''n''</sub>(''K''{{hairsp}}) to ''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>/{{hairsp}}[''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>,&thinsp;''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup>] with the reduced norm ''N''<sub>1</sub> from GL<sub>1</sub>(''K''{{hairsp}}) = ''K''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup> to ''F''<sup>{{hairsp}}×</sup> via the abelianization.

The '''Tannaka–Artin problem''' is whether these two maps have the same [[kernel (algebra)|kernel]] SL<sub>''n''</sub>(''K''{{hairsp}}).  This is true when ''F'' is locally compact<ref>{{cite journal | zbl=0060.07901 | last1=Nakayama | first1=Tadasi | last2=Matsushima | first2=Yozô | title=Über die multiplikative Gruppe einer p-adischen Divisionsalgebra | language=German | journal=Proc. Imp. Acad. Tokyo | volume=19 | pages=622–628 | year=1943 | doi=10.3792/pia/1195573246| doi-access=free }}</ref> but false in general.<ref>{{cite journal | zbl=0338.16005 | last=Platonov | first=V.P. | authorlink=Vladimir Platonov | title=The Tannaka-Artin problem and reduced K-theory | language=Russian | journal=Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR Ser. Mat. | volume=40 | pages=227–261 | year=1976 | issue=2 | doi=10.1070/IM1976v010n02ABEH001686 | bibcode=1976IzMat..10..211P }}</ref>
